long_biography.plain_text:
Molina began as an office assistant at Kodak while studying at Mexico's Escuela Bancaria y Comercial. By 22 he was managing for Pepsi, and at 28 took charge of a failing Guerrero bottler. He turned it around, acquired the franchise gradually and built a regional network before buying EMSA in Mexico City in 1984. That purchase became the foundation of Gemex.

Through further acquisitions and a later alliance with PepsiCo, Gemex became the company's anchor bottler in Mexico. Molina also assembled Consorcio Azucarero Escorpión, linking bottling with a major sugar-production business, but that group later encountered debt and government expropriations. In 2002, Pepsi Bottling Group offered for all Gemex shares; Molina and his affiliates agreed to tender their roughly 40 percent holding, ending his leadership of the bottler.
